object.title: Polynomial-time approximation conjecture for two-row Buttons & Scissors boards
object.statement:
A full **$2\times n$ board** is a board with two rows and $n$ columns, initially containing a button in every cell; the board has **$C=2$ colors** when its buttons use two colors. Here, $s$ denotes a constant independent of $n$.

**Two-row Buttons & Scissors conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm that removes all but $s$ buttons from any full $2\times n$ board with $C=2$ colors, for some constant $s$.

This conjecture concerns the unresolved algorithmic complexity of restricted one-player Buttons & Scissors puzzles. It asserts that boards with two rows and two colors can always be reduced to a constant number of remaining buttons in polynomial time, rather than necessarily solved completely.

Hearn, Adam Hesterberg, Michael Hoffmann, Hiro Ito, Irina Kostitsyna, Jody Leonard, Maarten Löffler, Aaron Santiago, Christiane Schmidt, Ryuhei Uehara, Yushi Uno and Aaron Williams, “Single-Player and Two-Player Buttons & Scissors Games”, arXiv:1607.01826 (2016).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

object.title: Graham--Sloane harmonious tree conjecture
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices. A harmonious labelling assigns distinct vertex labels and gives an edge $uv$ the label $(\psi(u)+\psi(v))\bmod(n-1)$. **Harmonious Tree Conjecture.** For any $n$-vertex tree $T$ there exists an injective labelling

$$
\psi:V(T) \rightarrow [n]
$$

such that the values

$$
\Big(\psi(u)+\psi(v)\mod (n-1)\Big)_{uv\in E(T)}
$$

are pairwise distinct. This is the harmonious analogue of the graceful tree conjecture, introduced by Graham and Sloane; the source gives no resolution and the problem remains open.
object.source_name: Anna Adamaszek, Peter Allen, Codrut Grosu and Jan Hladky, “Almost all trees are almost graceful”, arXiv:1608.01577 (2019).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2016).

object.title: The Circuit Double Cover Conjecture of Szekeres and Seymour
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-edge-connected graph, and let a **circuit double cover** be a family of circuits in which every edge of $G$ is covered twice. **Circuit Double Cover Conjecture.** Every 2-edge-connected graph has a family of circuits which covers every edge twice.

This is a longstanding conjecture in graph theory. The source states that the Shortest Circuit Cover Conjecture implies it, and that by Fleischner's splitting lemma it suffices to establish it for 2-edge-connected cubic graphs.
object.source_name: Yezhou Wu and Dong Ye, “Circuit Covers of Cubic Signed Graphs”, arXiv:1609.03620 (2016).

object.title: Aharoni–Berger–Chudnovsky–Howard–Seymour rainbow matching conjecture
object.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. A **rainbow matching** for a family of matchings is a matching whose edges are chosen from distinct members of the family. **Rainbow matching conjecture.** If $n$ is even, any $2n$ matchings of size $n$ in any graph have a rainbow matching of size $n$, and if $n$ is odd, any $2n-1$ matchings of size $n$ have a rainbow matching of size $n$. This conjecture generalizes Drisko's theorem from bipartite graphs to general graphs; the asserted bounds are motivated by the sharp bipartite result and the extremal example with $2n-2$ matchings. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

object.title: The linear-time conjecture for detecting rooted $K_4(X)$ or $W_4(X)$ minors
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $K_4(X)$- and $W_4(X)$-minors denote the rooted minor notions used in the source. **The rooted $K_4(X)$–$W_4(X)$ recognition conjecture.** There is a linear time algorithm for determining whether a graph $G$ has a $K_4(X)$-minor or $W_4(X)$-minor. object.title: Synchronization and large sets of Steiner systems in Johnson schemes
object.statement:
Let $J(n,k)$ be the Johnson scheme on the $k$-subsets of an $n$-set. A **large set** of Steiner systems is a collection of Steiner systems whose block sets partition all $k$-subsets. The Johnson scheme is **non-synchronizing** when the associated action fails to be synchronizing.

**Large-set conjecture.** There is a function $L$ such that, if $n\geqslant L(k)$, then the Johnson scheme $J(n,k)$ is non-synchronizing if and only if there exists a large set of Steiner triple systems $S(t,k,n)$ for some $t$ with $0<t<k$.

The conjecture links failure of synchronization to partitions of the $k$-subsets into Steiner-system block sets, while the preceding discussion relates such partitions to equality of clique and chromatic numbers.

object.title: Schaefer's bounded-crossing Hanani–Tutte conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph drawn on a surface $S$. The drawing is **independently even** if every pair of non-adjacent edges crosses an even number of times.

**Schaefer's conjecture.** If a graph $G$ has an independently even drawing on a surface $S$ such that every pair of edges crosses at most $t$ times, then $G$ has an embedding on $S$.

This is a weaker variant of the strong Hanani–Tutte theorem, parametrized by a positive integer $t$. The conjecture remains open for $t=1$.
object.source_name: Radoslav Fulek and Jan Kynčl, “Counterexample to an extension of the Hanani-Tutte theorem on the surface of genus 4”, arXiv:1709.00508 (2018).

object.title: Finite excluded-minor characterization for 3-connected constraint graphs with boundedly many islands
object.statement:
Let $k>1$. A **constraint graph with at most $k$ islands** is a constraint graph $(G,X)$ such that $G[X]$ has at most $k$ connected components.

**Finite excluded-minor conjecture.** The class of 3-connected constraint graphs with at most $k$ islands is characterised by a finite list of excluded constraint minors.

This proposes extending the paper's excluded-minor characterization from constraint connectedness to a bounded number of connected components. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

object.title: The gap conjecture for gapful bigraphs
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a bigraph. A bigraph is **gapful** when it has the gap property associated with the variable version Lovász local lemma, and $H$ **contains** a bigraph $H'$ when $H'$ can be embedded in $H$ by injections on the left and right vertex sets without incurring extra dependency. A bigraph $H'$ is **cyclic** if it contains a cycle.

**Gap conjecture.** A bigraph is gapful if and only if it contains a cyclic bigraph.

This conjecture proposes that containing a cyclic bigraph exactly characterizes gapfulness. The supplied text gives the decision result and the fact that every bigraph containing a cyclic one is gapful; the converse is presented as a natural conjecture and is not resolved in the supplied material.

object.title: The signed planar graph 4-colourability conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **signature** of $G$ is a mapping $\sigma:E(G)\to\{1,-1\}$. A **signed graph** is a pair $(G,\sigma)$, and it is **signed planar** when $G$ is planar. A $4$-colouring is a mapping satisfying the signed-graph colouring condition with four colours.

**Signed planar graph 4-colourability conjecture.** Every signed planar graph is $4$-colourable.

This conjecture strengthens the four colour theorem to signed graphs and was proposed by Máčajová, Raspaud and Škoviera. Its resolution status is not specified in the source.

object.title: High-girth Ramsey graph conjecture for ordered forests
object.statement:
Let $H$ and $H'$ be ordered forests, and let $t$ be a positive integer. Write $R_<(H,H')$ for the family of Ramsey graphs of $(H,H')$, and let $\operatorname{girth}(F)$ denote the girth of a graph $F$. **High-girth Ramsey graph conjecture.** There is an $F\in R_<(H,H')$ such that

$$
\operatorname{girth}(F)\geq t.
$$

This would extend the corresponding high-girth Ramsey-graph property from unordered forests to ordered forests; the paper presents it as an expected fact, and no resolution is given.

object.title: The complete-bipartite super-graceful classification conjecture
object.statement:
Let $K(m,n)$ be the complete bipartite graph with part sizes $m$ and $n$, and let $k$-super graceful have the labeling meaning used in the paper. **Complete-bipartite classification conjecture.** If $m=1$ and $n$ is prime, or if $n\geq m\geq 2$, then

$$
K(m,n)\text{ is $k$-super graceful if and only if }k\in\{1,m,n\}.
$$

This would classify the permitted parameters for the stated complete bipartite graphs; the source provides partial results but does not resolve the conjecture.
object.source_name: Gee-Choon Lau, Wai-Chee Shiu, Ho-Kuen Ng, Zhen-Bin Gao and Karl Schaffer, “Further Results On k-Super Graceful Graphs”, arXiv:1807.01188 (2021).

object.title: The complete multipartite super-graceful classification conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a complete $t$-partite graph, meaning that its vertex set is partitioned into $t$ independent parts and every two vertices in different parts are adjacent. Let $K(1,m,r)$ denote the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $1,m,r$. **Complete multipartite classification conjecture.** For $t\geq 3$, $G$ is $k$-super graceful if and only if

$$
G=K(1,m,r)\quad\text{and}\quad k=1.
$$

The source notes that the $k=1$ case for $K(1,m,r)$ is known, while the full classification remains conjectural.

object.title: Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture on cycle–clique Ramsey numbers
object.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices, $K_m$ the complete graph on $m$ vertices, and let $R(G,H)$ denote the two-colour Ramsey number of graphs $G$ and $H$. **Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture.** If

$$
n\geq m\geq 3,
$$

then

$$
R(C_n,K_m)=(n-1)(m-1)+1.
$$

The conjecture is a central question in Ramsey goodness for cycles. It is known for $n\geq 4m+2$ and for several small values of $m$, but remains open in general.
object.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Ramsey goodness of cycles”, arXiv:1807.02313 (2018).

object.title: Erdős's weak Dirac conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}\subset \mathbb{P}^{2}_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a finite set of mutually distinct $n$ points, and let $\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{P})$ be the set of lines determined by pairs of points of $\mathcal{P}$. **Erdős's weak Dirac conjecture.** Every set $\mathcal{P}$ of $n$ non-collinear points in the plane (presumably over the real numbers) contains a point which is incident to at least

$$
\left\lceil \frac{n}{c} \right\rceil
$$

lines from $\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{P})$ for a certain constant $c>0$. This is a classical incidence-geometric conjecture asserting the existence of a point incident to linearly many determined lines; the source does not provide evidence of a resolution.
object.source_name: Piotr Pokora, “Hirzebruch-type inequalities viewed as tools in combinatorics”, arXiv:1808.09167 (2020).
object.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09167

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2018). “A famous open problem due to Terao asks whether the freeness is combinatorial in nature.”

object.title: Separation conjecture for list arborability and equitable list arborability
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $k\in\mathbb{N}$. A graph is **$k$-list arborable** if every $k$-uniform list assignment admits a list colouring whose colour classes induce acyclic graphs. Suppose also that $G$ has a $k$-colouring in which every colour class has cardinality at most

$$
\left\lceil \frac{|V(G)|}{k}\right\rceil
$$

and induces an acyclic graph.

**Separation conjecture.** There is a graph $G$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfying both properties above, but $G$ is not equitably $k$-list arborable.

The conjecture asserts that ordinary list arborability together with an equitable acyclic colouring need not imply equitable list arborability. The source proposes it as an open question without a resolution.

object.title: Sharp logarithmic blowup-size conjecture for Erdős–Stone type results
object.statement:
Fix integers $r\geq s\geq 3$ and $\epsilon>0$. In the Erdős–Stone type result under discussion, $m$ denotes the number of edges and $t$ denotes the size of the blowup. **Sharp logarithmic blowup-size conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_{r,s,\epsilon}>0$ such that it is always possible to take

$$
t\geq c_{r,s,\epsilon}\log m,
$$

and this lower bound is best possible up to a constant factor. The conjecture asks for the optimal dependence of the blowup size on the number of edges, analogous to the logarithmic dependence in the Erdős–Stone theorem; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

object.title: Havet–Thomassé leaf-sensitive oriented-tree unavoidability conjecture
object.statement: An **oriented tree** is an orientation of an undirected tree, a leaf is a vertex of degree one in its underlying tree, and a digraph is $m$-unavoidable if it is contained as a subdigraph in every tournament of order $m$. **Havet–Thomassé's conjecture.** Every oriented tree of order $n$ with $k$ leaves is $(n+k-1)$-unavoidable. The conjecture is presented as stronger than Sumner's conjecture and remains open in the source; the paper proves several weaker bounds and establishes it for arborescences.

object.title: Burr's universality conjecture for oriented trees
object.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. An **oriented tree** is an orientation of a tree. A digraph is **$n$-universal** if it is contained in every $n$-chromatic digraph.

**Burr's conjecture.** Every oriented tree of order $n$ is $(2n-2)$-universal.

This is a generalization of Sumner's conjecture, which asserts that every oriented tree of order $n$ is contained in every tournament of order $2n-2$. The supplied text gives no evidence resolving Burr's stronger universality conjecture.

object.title: Linear degree-boundedness conjecture for pivot-minor exclusions
object.statement: For a positive integer $s$, a graph is **$K_{s,s}$-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $K_{s,s}$. **Linear pivot-minor degree-boundedness conjecture.** For each bipartite graph $H$, there exists a constant $C_H>0$ such that every $K_{s,s}$-free graph excluding $H$ as a pivot-minor has average degree at most $C_Hs$. This is the proposed pivot-minor analogue of Du and McCarty's vertex-minor conjecture; it is stated among the paper's open problems and no resolution is supplied.
